verdict.line: You lose if you stand in extended auto trades and let Mordekaiser bank three passive hits; you win if you dump Grit/W on a clean E-stun and disengage before he resets.

brief.thesis: Both champions scale off a resource they fill passively — Sett's Grit meter (W) builds from damage taken, Mordekaiser's passive aura builds from landing three hits — so this lane is a race to detonate your own meter before the enemy's finishes charging. Even at 51% over 3116 games because neither side has a clean counter to the other's burst window, just a better or worse read on when it opens.

theirWindow.when: Mordekaiser has landed 2+ hits on you
theirWindow.what: He's one auto or spell from the passive aura and move speed proc. Back off instead of trading the third hit — eating it lets him snowball the exchange with bonus damage and speed.

yourWindow.when: Your W (Haymaker) Grit meter is near full
yourWindow.what: Grit is stored from damage taken and dumped on cast for a shield plus true damage in the center, physical on the sides. Walk Mordekaiser into the center hitbox and release — this is your highest-value burst, not a poke tool.

powerCurve.note: Both poke-limited; neither stun nor passive aura online yet
Q maxed by 5, two empowered autos punish his melee range
His R unlocks a kill window before yours matches it
Both ultimates live, fight decided by execution

start.why: 82% pick at 51.8% win rate — the sustain and AD feed Sett's auto-reliant passive and Q trades better than the shield variant does against Mordekaiser's magic poke.

boots.why: 59.8% pick at 53% win rate — magic resist answers his Q/E/R magic damage, and tenacity shortens how long you're locked down after his E pull or R drag.

core.why: The active's slow and AoE auto let you stick through his W shield window and force the E-stun combo instead of chasing.
Shreds armor so your Q max-health damage and auto trades keep scaling as he builds tankier off his own W shield.
This exact path (Stridebreaker into Black Cleaver into Sterak's Gage) runs 68.8% over 96 games — the tenacity and health keep you alive through his R stat-steal all-in.

situational.when: mordekaiser is landing full E-into-R combos and you need more raw HP and magic resist to survive the all-in
the lane stays even past level 11 and turns into a sustained auto-trade war rather than burst windows
you're ahead and want faster Q/W/E cooldowns to cycle Grit and the stun more often

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror stacks through the extended trades this lane forces and converts to healing at max stacks, which matches dumping Grit into an all-in rather than one-off pokes.

summoners.why: 92.4% pick at 51.5% win rate — Ignite punishes his W by burning through the health he'd otherwise bank into a shield, and secures kills off your E-stun or R combo before he can W-heal back.

playing.title: Deny his passive stacks
playing.detail: Hit-and-run rather than standing in extended trades. Every third hit he lands on you procs his damage aura and move speed — don't give him the free third hit.

playing.title: Dump W on the true-damage center
playing.detail: Haymaker's center hits true damage, the sides only physical. Walk him into the middle before releasing stored Grit, not just whichever side is closest.

playing.title: Save E for isolated angles
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are pulled from opposite sides; a one-sided pull just slows. Only commit E when Mordekaiser is alone, not grouped with minions on one flank.

playing.title: Close with Q, not autos alone
playing.detail: Q's move speed toward champions plus two empowered attacks dealing max-health damage is how you win the gap-close into melee range instead of trading autos on his terms.

playing.title: Track his W shield state
playing.detail: Indestructible banks damage dealt and taken into a shield he can pop to heal. Time your all-in for right after he's consumed it, not while it's stacked.

playing.title: Isolate before using R
playing.detail: The Show Stopper carries one enemy through the air alone — use it to pull Mordekaiser away from allies before his own Realm of Death can drag you first.

playing.title: Respect his longer E range
playing.detail: Death's Grasp reaches 700 range against your Facebreaker's 490. Don't walk into his pull range before your Grit or W is ready to answer.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Try to hit and run often to prevent Mordekaiser from activating his (P). Try to hit him at the center part of [W] when dealing damage.
